request.spec: When no registration date is supplied, set it to the server's current date and return 'registrationDate' in ISO format 'YYYY-MM-DD'.
request.prompt:
Implement the following change to the application so that it fully satisfies
the specification and all existing and new tests pass. Run the test suite and
make it green before finishing.

When no registration date is supplied, set it to the server's current date and return 'registrationDate' in ISO format 'YYYY-MM-DD'.

code_review.final_verdict:
VERDICT: CHANGES REQUESTED

The field, accessors, schema columns, and OpenAPI additions are all clean and idiomatic. The one structural issue is where the defaulting logic lives.

**Default-date logic is at the wrong altitude (web layer instead of persistence/service layer).**

`OwnerRestControllerV1.addOwner` now does:
```java
if (owner.getRegistrationDate() == null) {
    owner.setRegistrationDate(LocalDate.now());
}
```
This is a persistence/domain default — "a newly saved owner gets today's date" — being applied in the controller. In this codebase that concern already has a natural home: `ClinicServiceImpl.saveOwner` (`src/main/java/.../service/ClinicServiceImpl.java:235`) is where pre-save domain rules live (`assertTelephoneIsUnique(owner)` sits right there). Defaulting `registrationDate` is the same kind of save-time rule and belongs beside it, not in the controller.

Why this matters structurally:
- **Thin controllers.** The controllers here are deliberately thin pass-throughs (map DTO → entity → `clinicService.saveOwner` → map back). This change makes V1 the only controller carrying business defaulting logic.
- **Single entry point / no future duplication.** There is a parallel `OwnerRestControllerV2` (`.../rest/controller/v2/OwnerRestControllerV2.java`) which currently only lists owners. If/when V2 gains a create endpoint, the default would have to be copy-pasted into it. Putting the default in `saveOwner` (the single choke point every create path already goes through) makes it apply uniformly with no duplication.

Suggested change: move the null-check/default into `ClinicServiceImpl.saveOwner` (guarded by `owner.getRegistrationDate() == null`, so updates of an already-dated owner are unaffected since the loaded entity's date is non-null), and drop the `LocalDate` import and the block from `OwnerRestControllerV1`.

(A JPA `@PrePersist` callback on `Owner` would also be idiomatic and would fire only on insert, but there is no existing `@PrePersist` precedent in this codebase, whereas the service layer already owns pre-save rules — so the service is the more codebase-natural home here.)
